raw_response:
I am 59 this year, and I have been farming this land since I was 14 — forty-five years. My farm is only 9 mu, divided into 4 mu of cotton and 5 mu of spring maize. It is not big, but it is what we have. My husband is 62 and his back is not what it used to be, so he mostly helps with decisions and light work around the yard. Our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for planting and harvest, so day-to-day it is mostly me out in the fields.

Right now it is late April, so I need to get both crops in the ground soon. For the cotton, I am planting guoxinmian, the same variety I have used for three years. It has done well — last year I got about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton, and the price was around 3.5 yuan per jin. I still have some seed I saved from last year, but I bought a little fresh seed too, about 3 jin per mu, to make sure the germination is good. Cotton is a lot of work. I have to thin the seedlings, prune the branches, top the plants, spray for insects all summer, and pick three or four times. At my age, the bending and picking gets harder every year. This year I will hire Auntie Wang's nephew to help with the topping and the main picking — I will pay him about 100 yuan a day for maybe 8 days total. 

For fertilizer on the cotton, the extension agent last winter said I could cut back to about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, but I have always used about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that is 50 kg — and then another half bag at flowering time in July. The compound I buy is around 20-10-10, so that is about 15 kg of nitrogen total. I know it is a bit more than what the book says, but I remember 2019 when my neighbor Li tried to save 50 yuan on fertilizer and his cotton turned yellow and stunted. He lost half his yield. I would rather waste a little money on fertilizer than risk that. I also put down some farmyard manure when I have it, but this year I only had enough for the vegetable patch by the house.

For the spring maize, I am planting zhengdan 958, a hybrid. It costs me about 45 yuan per mu for the seed, but it is worth it — the yield is steady. I will plant it in the first week of May, right after I finish the cotton planting. The maize is easier to manage. I will rotary till the field, spread one bag of compound fertilizer — the same 20-10-10, about 50 kg per mu — plant the seeds, and then the main jobs are weeding and one topdressing with urea at jointing in late June. If the maize looks yellow, I might add a bit more, but usually one topdressing is enough.

Water is expensive here. We pump from the tube well and it is metered — about 50 yuan per mu each time I irrigate. Last year I irrigated the cotton three times, but the pump has been slower this spring and I heard the water table is dropping, so I am planning two times for cotton and once for the maize unless July is very dry. Every yuan matters. Our son sends some money back each month, but we still need to keep some cash in hand for emergencies. My husband's medicine costs add up.

For pests, cotton needs the most attention. I will spray herbicide once after planting, and then insecticide maybe 10 or 12 times through the summer — the bollworm always comes, and the aphids. For the maize, one round of herbicide after planting is usually enough, and I only spray insecticide if I see damage.

I expect about 260 kg per mu from the cotton and about 500 kg per mu from the maize if the weather is normal. Last year was dry in June and the maize suffered a little, so I am being a bit conservative. Total costs this year — seed, fertilizer, irrigation, pesticide, and the hired help for cotton — will run to about 3,200 yuan. That is a big chunk of our cash, but if I do not put in the inputs, I do not get the output. That is the way it is.
